text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz BALDWIN RESTAURANT GROUP Modern plates. Proper pours. OUR STORY A family restaurant group built on hospitality first. Three restaurants, one family, and a standard that started in 2004. Shelby Township, MI Since 2004 Where we came from OUR HISTORY In 2004, after more than two decades in some of Metro Detroit’s most respected kitchens, Chef Jeff Baldwin and Rosemarie Baldwin opened J.Baldwin’s in Clinton Township. The idea: fine-dining flavor and technique in a room that feels welcoming. It grew into a true family business. Testa Barra followed in Macomb Township, and The Baldwin is next, carrying the same values: hospitality, consistency and bringing people together. 2004 J.Baldwin’s opens Chef Jeff and Rosemarie Baldwin, Clinton Township 2016 Baldwin Restaurant Group is formed The family business becomes a group 2017 Testa Barra opens Chefs Mike and Gabriella Baldwin, Macomb Township NEXT The Baldwin opens Shelby Township · date to add A true family business THE BALDWIN FAMILY Chef Jeff Baldwin Founder and chef. text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz The Bar / Bar basics / How guests order Speak the language HOW GUESTS ORDER Guests order in shorthand. Know what every word means, how to make it, and when to ask a follow-up question. WHEN IN DOUBT “Neat, or chilled and up?” Ask whenever a guest says “straight.” Know every word THE WORDS THEY SAY IT MEANS WE SERVE IT Neat A spirit at room temperature. No ice, nothing added. Rocks glass or Glencairn, no ice. On the rocks Poured over ice. Rocks glass with ice. A big cube for whiskey. Up / straight up Shaken or stirred with ice, then strained. No ice in the glass. Chilled coupe, Nick & Nora or martini glass. Straight Can mean neat or up. Guests use it both ways. Always ask: “Neat, or chilled and up?” Double Twice the spirit, same amount of mixer. Ring it as a double. It costs more. Double neat A double pour of spirit, no ice. Rocks glass or snifter, no ice. Tall More mixer in a taller glass. Same spirit. Highball or Collins. Short Less mixer in a smaller glass. Rocks glass. Dirty Olive brine added, usually to a martini. Ask how dirty: a little or extra. Dry / extra dry Less vermouth in a martini. Extra dry

name: Bar Basics · Shaken vs Stirred
title: Shaken vs Stirred
blurb: How a drink is mixed changes how it tastes, looks and feels. One simple rule covers most cocktails.
text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz The Bar / Bar basics / Shaken vs. stirred Method matters SHAKEN VS. STIRRED How a drink is mixed changes how it tastes, looks and feels. One simple rule covers most cocktails. THE RULE Shake if it has citrus, juice, egg, dairy or cream. Stir if it’s all spirits. Hard and fast SHAKEN WHEN Citrus, juice, egg, dairy or cream WHAT IT DOES Chills fast, adds air and water. Makes a lively, frothy, slightly cloudy drink. HOW LONG 10–15 seconds, hard, until the tin frosts. TOOLS Shaker tins, Hawthorne strainer, fine strainer. Margarita Daiquiri Whiskey Sour Cosmopolitan Espresso Martini Smooth and slow STIRRED WHEN All spirits, no juice WHAT IT DOES Chills gently with no air. Keeps the drink clear, silky and heavy. HOW LONG 20–30 seconds, until the mixing glass is ice-cold. TOOLS Mixing glass, bar spoon, julep strainer. Old Fashioned Manhattan Martini Negroni Sazerac Beyond the shake OTHER METHODS Built Made right in the glass, over ice. No shaker. Paloma Moscow Mule Aperol Spritz Muddled Fruit, herbs or sugar pressed gently to release flavor. Mojito Dry shake Shaken without ice first, to whip egg white into foam

text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz Wine / Wine service / Present the bottle STEP 01 Present Wine service · 1 of 6 Show it before you open it PRESENT THE BOTTLE Show the host the bottle before you open it, so they can confirm it’s the wine they ordered. title: Open sparkling
blurb: A sparkling bottle is under high pressure. Open it with a quiet sigh, never a pop, and never point it at…
text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz Wine / Wine service / Open sparkling STEP 03 Sparkling Wine service · 3 of 6 A sigh, not a pop OPEN SPARKLING A sparkling bottle is under high pressure. Open it with a quiet sigh, never a pop, and never point it at anyone. TOOLS A napkin TIME About a minute WHEN Well chilled, at the table CHECK Point it away from people 1 Present 2 Open 3 Sparkling 4 Taste 5 Pour 6 Decant How to do it STEP BY STEP 1 Remove the foil. 2 Put your thumb on the cork and keep it there. 3 Loosen the wire cage, but leave it on the cork. 4 Tilt the bottle 45°, pointed away from guests. 5 Hold the cork and cage still, and slowly turn the bottle. 6 Let the gas out with a quiet hiss. ALWAYS ✓ Keep your thumb on the cork ✓ Point away from guests and lights ✓ Chill it well first NEVER ✕ Pop the cork ✕ Let go once the cage is loose ✕ Shake the bottle SAY IT AT THE TABLE “Cheers! May I pour for the table?” i GOOD TO KNOW A sparkling wine bottle holds several times the pressure of a car tire. A loose cork can cause a serious injury. title: The host taste

text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz Wine / Wine service / The host taste STEP 04 Taste Wine service · 4 of 6 Check it before you pour THE HOST TASTE Pour a small taste for the host, so they can check the wine is sound before you serve the table. TOOLS A clean glass TIME About 30 seconds WHEN After opening, before pouring CHECK A corked smell 1 Present 2 Open 3 Sparkling 4 Taste 5 Pour 6 Decant How to do it STEP BY STEP 1 Pour about 1 oz for the host. 2 Step back and wait. 3 When they approve, pour for the table. 4 If they say something is wrong, smell it yourself. 5 Bring the manager or sommelier. Never argue. ALWAYS ✓ Pour a small taste ✓ Stay calm and kind ✓ Offer a fresh bottle if it’s faulty NEVER ✕ Argue with the guest ✕ Pour the table before approval ✕ Taste from the guest’s glass What can go wrong KNOW THE FAULTS Corked Wet cardboard, musty basement. Oxidized Brown, flat, tastes like sherry. Heat damaged Stewed, jammy, cork pushed up. Too warm or cold Not a fault. Chill or let it rest. SAY IT AT THE TABLE “Would you like to taste?” If there’s a problem: “I’m sorry about that. Let me get you a fresh bottle.” i GOOD TO KNOW Corked win

title: Pour for the table
blurb: Pour for the whole table the same amount each time, from each guest’s right, finishing with the host.
text: Search dishes, ingredients, allergens… Opening Menu · Fall 2026 Pre-Shift Quiz Wine / Wine service / Pour for the table STEP 05 Pour Wine service · 5 of 6 Even, clean, host last POUR FOR THE TABLE Pour for the whole table the same amount each time, from each guest’s right, finishing with the host. TOOLS A napkin POUR About 5 oz WHEN After the host approves CHECK Even pours, no drips 1 Present 2 Open 3 Sparkling 4 Taste 5 Pour 6 Decant How to do it STEP BY STEP 1 Pour from each guest’s right, moving clockwise. 2 Serve the guests first and the host last. 3 Fill to the widest part of the glass, about 5 oz. 4 Pour sparkling slowly, in two passes. 5 Twist the bottle as you finish to stop drips. 6 Set the bottle down label out, or in an ice bucket. ALWAYS ✓ Twist to stop drips ✓ Keep pours even ✓ Watch glasses and offer more NEVER ✕ Fill a glass to the top ✕ Touch the bottle to the glass ✕ Let the table run dry without asking SAY IT AT THE TABLE “May I top that off for you?” i GOOD TO KNOW A 750 ml bottle pours about five 5 oz glasses. Count heads before you pour so it comes out even. PART OF Wine service PREVIOUS The host taste NEXT Decanting
